publications.title: How You Mark It Matters: Particle-Level Framing Effects in a Korean Search Agent
publications.venue: Annual Conference on Human & Cognitive Language Technology (HCLT 2026)
publications.tldr: Rewording a question with a different Korean particle leaves a search agent's verdict unchanged, but silently swaps out most of the evidence behind it. We sent 60 health-science claims under six framings to Liner's production search agent (4,510 API calls) and had 1,200 answers labeled blind by human annotators. Meaning-preserving particle swaps had no measurable effect on verdicts, yet replaced 84-86% of the scholarly sources retrieved. Explicitly directional framing flipped the verdict on 53% of claims, almost all of them contested or emerging, while the retrieved sources stayed 96.4% identical: the flip happens when the answer is generated, not when evidence is retrieved.

publications.title: Multimodal Deep Learning Model for Prediction of Prognosis in Central Nervous System Inflammation
publications.tldr: Brain MRI and clinical data together predict the outcome of CNS inflammation better than either alone. A 3D CNN reads 43 brain regions segmented from T1-weighted MRI with FastSurfer, and its features are fused with clinical variables. Trained on 291 patients and tested on a later, held-out cohort of 106, the multimodal model beat single-modality models in every cause group (external AUROC 0.80 autoimmune, 0.91 bacterial, 0.92 viral, 1.00 tuberculosis). Shown the model's output, neurologists, paediatricians and radiologists all predicted prognosis more accurately.

publications.title: Self-Claimed Authority Cues and Application-Layer Fact Verification in a Korean-Language Commercial Generative Search API
publications.tldr: Tell a Korean search agent you work at the institution in question, and it becomes far more likely to accept your false claim; one added instruction undoes that. Across 15 cases in five domains (education, government policy, companies, transport, culture), each checkable against official sources, we put false claims to Liner's Search Agent API in multi-turn conversations. Plain false claims were accepted 42.2% of the time; with a self-claimed insider cue, 93.3%. Asking afterwards for the claim to be judged against official sources corrected 61.9–73.7% of those acceptances, and the same instruction sent alongside the false claim prevented acceptance entirely, with or without the cue. An exploratory result (one API, 15 cases), but a defence developers can add at the request level without retraining anything.

publications.title: Deep learning model for the prognostic prediction of acute inflammation of the central nervous system using T2-weighted brain magnetic resonance imaging
publications.tldr: Can a routine T2-weighted brain MRI alone predict how patients with acute CNS inflammation will be doing at discharge? A modified 3D DenseNet trained on scans of 483 Severance Hospital patients from 2010–2019 predicted a poor outcome (modified Rankin Scale ≥ 3) in a later 2020–2023 cohort with an AUROC of 0.78 and accuracy of 0.82. Separate models per cause of inflammation gave mixed results (AUROC 0.87 for autoimmune, 0.65–0.67 for bacterial and viral), which pointed toward adding clinical information in a multimodal model.

publications.title: Development of an Artificial Intelligence Model for Diagnosis and Classification of Idiopathic Generalized Epilepsy using 3D Brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging
publications.tldr: Two forms of idiopathic generalized epilepsy, juvenile myoclonic epilepsy (JME) and generalized tonic-clonic seizures alone (GTCA), look so alike clinically that even specialists struggle to tell them apart. From 3D T1-weighted MRI of 196 people (127 JME, 37 GTCA, 32 healthy controls), a DenseNet-169-based model reading 43 FastSurfer-segmented brain regions separated the three groups with a macro-average AUROC of 0.81, although their clinical variables showed no significant differences. SHAP highlighted the parietal lobe and deep structures including the thalamus, amygdala and basal ganglia, partly matching earlier radiomics and fMRI findings.

publications.title: A device for providing an early classification and prognosis prediction model for central nervous system inflammatory diseases based on multimodal deep learning, and its control method
publications.tldr: A device and method for predicting the prognosis of CNS inflammatory disease from a patient's MRI combined with their clinical information, using SHAP values to choose what the model learns from. The brain is split into 43 regions, grouped into 14 categories, and the 10 with the highest SHAP values are kept for training, with a separate model for each cause of disease; the output is a prediction of disability or no disability. The claims also cover the SHAP estimator itself, which averages Monte Carlo samples over coalition vectors and checks the result for local additivity.
